steps.body: A prime number has exactly two factors: 1 and itself. A composite has more, which means it can be built as a rectangle with both sides above 1.
steps.narration: A prime number has exactly two factors: 1 and itself. A composite has more, which means it can be built as a rectangle with both sides above 1.

widget.prompt: 15 is composite. Build it as a rectangle with both sides greater than 1.
widget.successFeedback: 15 — a 5 by 3 rectangle, which is exactly what makes 15 composite.
widget.lowFeedback: Smaller than 15 — keep building to the full area.
widget.highFeedback: Larger than 15 — a side has grown past the pair asked for.
widget.factorFeedback: That area is right, but 1 by 15 is the pair every number has; composite means a pair with BOTH sides above 1.

predict.prompt: Can 13 be built as a rectangle with both sides above 1?
predict.reveal: 13's only factors are 1 and 13, so the only rectangle is the 1-wide strip — the signature of a prime.

steps.body: Show a different composite number with a whole-number rectangle whose sides are both above 1.

widget.prompt: 21 is composite. Build it as a rectangle with sides 7 and 3.
widget.successFeedback: 21 — 7 by 3 has two sides above 1, which proves 21 is composite.
widget.lowFeedback: Smaller than 21 — keep building until the rectangle covers all 21 squares.
widget.highFeedback: Larger than 21 — reduce a side until the area is exactly 21.
widget.factorFeedback: That area is right, but this proof uses the 7 by 3 rectangle.

steps.body: Rule out a nontrivial factor pair.

widget.prompt: Only 1 × 11 builds 11. Is 11 prime or composite?

options.label: Prime
options.feedback: Correct — 11 has no factors besides 1 and itself, so the only rectangle it builds is 1 by 11.

options.label: Composite
options.feedback: 11 has no factor pair other than 1 and 11, so it cannot be composed of smaller whole-number sides.
